chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shammun narrated to me; he said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to me; he said:

I wrote to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) when al-Muhtadī had begun killing the mawālī: “O my master, praise belongs to Allah, who has preoccupied him away from us. It has reached me that he is threatening you and saying: ‘By Allah, I will surely expel them from the face of the earth.’”
So Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) wrote in his own hand: “That is shorter for his lifespan. Count five days from this day of yours.”
“And he will be killed on the sixth day, after humiliation and abasement that will befall him.” So it happened just as he (عليه السلام) had said.

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, the kunyah of Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام)
key_terms.اسْتِخْفَافٍ: belittlement or abasement that would befall him
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: the mawali, referring here to those being targeted and killed
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدِي: al-Muhtadi, the Abbasid caliph mentioned in the report
key_terms.لِعُمُرِهِ: for his lifespan, indicating the shortening of al-Muhtadi’s life

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام) respond to al-Muhtadi’s threat?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a letter sent to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام) during the reign of al-Muhtadi, who was threatening the Imam and his followers. The Imam foretold that al-Muhtadi’s threat would hasten his end and that he would be killed on the sixth day after humiliation. The report highlights the Imam’s foreknowledge and occurs within a historical context of Abbasid oppression.

en.hubeali: Is’haq said, ‘Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun narrated to me saying, ‘Ahmad Bin Muhammad narrated to me saying,

‘I wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) when Al-Muhtady (the Caliph) took to the killing of the Slaves, ‘O my Master<sup>asws</sup>” The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Pre-occupied him from us<sup>asws</sup>, for it has reached me that he had threatened you<sup>asws</sup> and he was saying, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I shall remove them from the new land’.

So Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> signed by his<sup>asws</sup> own handwriting: ‘That would be a shortening for his life-span. Count five days from this day of yours, and he would be killed during the sixth day after humiliation and being belittled passing by’.
So it happened just as he<sup>asws</sup> had said’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ishaq has said that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan Shammun has said that Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me the following.

“I wrote to abu Muhammad (a.s.) when al-Muhtadi had began to kill the Turkish Mawali (slave or supporters). My master, we thank Allah for diverting his (al-Muhtadi’s) attention from us. I have heard that he had threatened you and has said, By Allah, I will wipe them out from the face of the earth.”
Abu Muhammad (a.s.) sent in response with his own signature. “This will be much shortening to his life. Count five days from today.
On the sixth day he will be killed with humiliation and insults that he will go through.” It then happned exactly as he had said.”
